transcript: Birdie
Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Mei-Ling Tan

Hi hi! I'm Mei-Ling, I own Spoke & Sprocket Bike Studio down in Katong! Nice to meet you 😊 So excited to figure this chatbot thing out, my customers keep asking me the same questions over and over and I never remember what I told the last person lol
Birdie

Nice to meet you too, Mei-Ling! That sounds like exactly the kind of thing a chatbot can fix. To start — can you tell me a bit about what Spoke & Sprocket does? Like, are you mainly selling bikes, doing repairs, rentals, classes... or a mix?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh okay so we're mainly custom bike builds, e-bike conversions (like turning a regular bike into electric, battery + motor swaps), and general repairs/tune-ups. That's the core of it! We're NOT doing rentals yet, though I keep thinking about it... maybe launching that soon actually, I have some space in the back I could use. But right now, it's really just build + convert + repair. Oh and my mechanic Rafiq handles most of the conversion stuff, he's the real expert there, I just do fittings and sales side of things!
Birdie

Got it — build, convert, repair, with Rafiq as your conversion guru and you handling fittings and sales. Good to know rentals might be coming later too, we can keep that in mind. Now, where do customers usually reach out to you with these repeat questions — is it WhatsApp, Instagram, phone calls, walk-ins, or something else?
Mei-Ling Tan

Mostly WhatsApp honestly! Some Instagram DMs too, and then walk-ins ask me the same stuff in person lol. Phone calls happen but less now, everyone just messages. Oh and sometimes people email but I forget to check that one for like days at a time 😅 so WhatsApp is really the main one, that's where I get hammered with "how much for a tune up" type questions
Birdie

That makes total sense — WhatsApp being the main hotspot for 'how much for a tune up' questions is such a common thing! Before we go further, it'd help me a lot to see a few real examples of these WhatsApp or Instagram conversations — actual questions customers ask you. If you have chat exports or screenshots, you can drop them in the 'uploads' folder next to this program and just tell me when you're done. Or if that's a hassle, you could just paste a few example messages right here in the chat. Either way works!
Mei-Ling Tan

Oh easy, let me just type some out instead of digging through my phone lol. Okay typical ones I get:

"hi how much for a basic tune up?" — and honestly I say S$45 sometimes, S$60 other times, depends on my mood I guess 😅

"how much to convert my bike to electric" — I usually say S$800-1400 depending on motor wattage

"do you guys open on Monday?" — no we're closed Mondays, 10-7 the rest of the week... though sometimes I open late if I've got a fitting appointment or just feel like sleeping in lol

"how long for e-bike conversion" — this one stresses me out because honestly could be 2 weeks could be 5 weeks, my Taiwan supplier is so unreliable right now

"do you do rentals" — I keep telling people yes next month but then... it just hasn't happened yet lol maybe I should stop saying that

That's like 90% of what I get asked!
Birdie

Ha, I love how honest you're being! 😄 Okay, real talk on the tune-up pricing — since it swings between S$45 and S$60, do you want the bot to just quote one fixed price to keep things consistent, or would you rather it give a range like the e-bike conversions?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh good question... okay let's just say S$50 flat, that's easy to remember! Actually wait — maybe S$50-60 range is safer in case Rafiq needs to charge more for like, really messed up gears or something. Ugh okay let's just do the range, S$50-60, that covers me either way 😅
Birdie
S$50-60 it is, nice and simple. Now what about custom bike builds — do those have a typical price range too, or does it vary too much case by case to quote?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh custom builds, okay so — starts around S$2,000, that's usually what I tell people! Though... hmm, I know I've said S$1,800 as a "starting from" to a few customers too, oops. Let's just go with S$2,000 as the starting point, that feels more accurate honestly. But it really can go way up depending on frame material, components, all that — so maybe bot should say "starting from S$2,000, final price depends on specs" or something like that? Yeah let's do that 😅
Birdie

Perfect, 'starting from S$2,000, final price depends on specs' is a great way to phrase it. Now let's talk bookings — when someone wants a custom build, an e-bike conversion, or even just a tune-up, how does that work right now? Do you take a deposit upfront, or is payment only when the work's done?
Mei-Ling Tan

Okay so for custom builds we do ask for a deposit — technically it's supposed to be 30% upfront. Though honestly I've waived it for regulars before, and then like the same week I told a new customer it's 50%... I know, I know, I need to just pick one 😅 Let's say 30% standard, and I can decide case by case if I want to waive it. For tune-ups and repairs, no deposit, you just pay when it's done!
Birdie

Got it, 30% standard deposit for custom builds with room for you to waive it case-by-case — that's a totally reasonable rule for the bot to know. What about e-bike conversions — is there a deposit for those too, or is it pay-on-completion like the tune-ups?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh hmm, good question — I think e-bike conversions should also need a deposit? Like since we have to order the parts from Taiwan and all, I don't wanna be stuck holding a S$1,200 motor kit if someone bails. So let's say... 30% same as custom builds? Actually wait, maybe higher, like 50%, because the parts cost is the bulk of it and I don't want to be out of pocket... ugh okay let's just say 30-50%, I'll decide depending on the customer 😅 sorry I know that's wishy washy!
Birdie

No worries at all, that's exactly the kind of thing we're sorting out now so the bot doesn't have to guess! I'll flag that deposit percentage as a to-decide item for later. Let's move to cancellations — if someone pays a deposit and then cancels, do you refund it, keep it, or is that also a case-by-case thing?
Mei-Ling Tan

Hmm, okay so... honestly I don't think I've ever written this down anywhere lol. I think if it's like, materials haven't been ordered yet, I'd refund it? But if Rafiq already ordered the parts or cut the frame, then no, I gotta keep it 'cause I'm out that money already. So maybe... refundable before we order stuff, non-refundable after? Ugh but honestly I've also just refunded people anyway even after ordering because I felt bad 😅 so... case by case-ish? Sorry that's probably not the answer you want!
Birdie

That's actually really helpful context, no need to apologize! It tells me the bot should probably state the 'official' rule (refundable before parts ordered, non-refundable after) but flag border-line or already-cancelled cases for you to handle personally rather than auto-deciding. Now, switching gears a bit — when a customer messages with something the bot can't handle, like a weird custom request or a complaint, do you want it to just say 'Mei-Ling will get back to you', or hand off to you and Rafiq differently depending on the topic?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh good question! I think... for anything conversion-related, weird motor questions or complaints about e-bike stuff, it should go to Rafiq, since he's the expert and I'll just fumble it. Everything else — builds, fittings, general "can you fix this weird thing" — comes to me.

Actually wait, no — maybe everything should just come to me first? Like even the technical stuff, I don't want customers messaging Rafiq directly and him being like "why is this rando texting me" lol. So maybe it's always "Mei-Ling will get back to you" and then I forward to Rafiq myself if it's technical?

Yeah let's do that, everything funnels to me first! Sorry, I flip-flopped mid sentence there 😅
Birdie
Got it, everything funnels to you first, easy rule to follow. Quick background question — how long has Spoke & Sprocket been running in Katong?
Mei-Ling Tan
Six years now! Opened the shop right here in Katong, feels like both forever and also like just yesterday lol. Time flies when you're covered in chain grease 😅
Birdie

Six years, that's awesome — clearly doing something right! 😄 So who's your typical customer — are you mostly serving casual neighborhood riders, serious cycling enthusiasts, commuters looking to go electric, or a mix of all of that?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh it's really a mix! Like we get the serious cyclists who want a full custom frame build, the everyday commuters who just want their bike to stop squeaking, and then a good chunk of people coming in specifically for e-bike conversions because they don't want to bike up sweaty to work anymore lol. Katong's got a lot of families too so sometimes it's parents getting their kid's bike fixed up. So yeah... honestly no single "type," we get everyone 😅
Birdie

Love that, sounds like Spoke & Sprocket is a real neighborhood fixture. Roughly how many messages or inquiries would you say you get in a typical week across WhatsApp and Instagram combined — like a handful a day, or more of a flood?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh let me think... probably like 15-20 a week? Just kind of steady, few a day. Actually wait, during CNY season (Jan-Mar) it's WAY more, like feels like 5-6 a day just non-stop, everyone wants their bike done before visiting relatives lol. So normal time maybe 15-20, but Jan-Mar could easily be double that. Sorry, is that a useless answer 😅 it really depends on the season!
Birdie

Not useless at all, that's super helpful — good to know CNY season basically doubles your load! Now, big picture question: do you want this chatbot to actually handle bookings and take deposits/payments itself, or would you rather it just answer questions and send reminders while you still handle the booking and payment side yourself?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh, big question! Um... I think I'd want it to just answer questions and maybe send reminders? Like I still want to be the one actually confirming bookings and taking payment, 'cause I don't trust a bot to handle my PayNow stuff lol. Actually wait — maybe for simple stuff like tune-up bookings it could just book the slot directly? Since that's low stakes. But for custom builds and deposits, no way, that needs to go through me.

Hmm actually... maybe even the tune-up bookings should come to me first too, just so I can double check my schedule isn't a mess that day 😅 ugh sorry, let's just say: bot answers questions + sends reminders, I handle all the actual booking/payment stuff myself. Safer that way!
Birdie

That's a smart, safer choice — answer questions and send reminders, you keep control of the actual booking and payment. Good to lock that in. Now, how will you know this chatbot is actually working well for you — like, is success 'I stop repeating myself all day,' or more like 'I get more bookings,' or something else?
Mei-Ling Tan

Haha honestly it's mostly "I stop repeating myself all day"! Like if I never have to type "we're closed Mondays" or "S$45-60 for a tune up" ever again in my life I'll be so happy 😅 More bookings would be nice too but really I just want my sanity back, I'm answering the same 5 questions on WhatsApp while trying to fit someone's handlebars, it's chaos lol. So yeah — success = less repetitive typing for me, that's the big one!
Birdie

I totally get that, answering handlebars questions while fitting handlebars sounds like a nightmare! Do you have a rough budget in mind for this chatbot project, or a timeline for when you'd like it up and running?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh budget, um... I haven't really thought hard about it lol. Maybe like S$100-150 a month? That feels reasonable for something that just answers questions. Actually wait, if it saves me hours every week maybe I'd go up to S$200? Ugh okay let's just say S$100-200 range, I'm flexible-ish 😅

Timeline-wise... ASAP honestly! Like before CNY season hits again would be amazing, that's when I'm drowning. So maybe... end of next month? Actually that might be too tight with my schedule being crazy. Let's just say "as soon as reasonably possible" and I'll try not to stress you out about it lol
Birdie

Sounds good, S$100-200/month and 'as soon as possible' noted! Quick one — since you're in Katong, do you get many customers who'd prefer chatting in Mandarin, Malay, or another language, or is English totally fine for everyone?
Mei-Ling Tan

Oh! Um, mostly English is fine honestly. Some of my older uncle-aunty customers do Mandarin, so maybe like... 10-15% of the time? But they usually just get one of us to translate in person or type simple English anyway lah. I don't think you need to build a whole Mandarin thing for this, English should cover like 90% of it 😊 unless that's easy to add anyway?
Birdie

Good to know, English-first with a light touch of Mandarin support if it's easy to add — we can note that as a nice-to-have. Last background question: do you use any booking or calendar tools already (like Google Calendar, an appointment app, etc.), or is everything currently just tracked in your head or a notebook?
Mei-Ling Tan

Haha it's really just... in my head mostly? 😅 Okay and a paper notebook by the register for appointments, super old school I know. Rafiq keeps his own conversion job list on like a whiteboard in the back too lol. I keep meaning to switch to Google Calendar or one of those apps but I never actually got around to it! So yeah — nothing digital right now, it's all vibes and handwriting 😂
Birdie

Alright Mei-Ling, I think I've got a full picture! Here's a summary of everything for you to double check:

**Business**: Spoke & Sprocket Bike Studio, Katong, 6 years running. You handle fittings/sales, Rafiq handles conversions/mechanics. No digital booking system yet — paper notebook + whiteboard.

**Services & Pricing**:
- Tune-up: S$50-60
- E-bike conversion: S$800-1,400 (depends on motor wattage)
- Custom build: starting from S$2,000, final price depends on specs

**Hours**: Closed Mondays, 10am-7pm Tue-Sun (sometimes later start if you have a fitting or just feel like it)

**Deposits & Cancellations**:
- Tune-ups/repairs: no deposit, pay on completion
- Custom builds: 30% deposit standard, waived sometimes for regulars
- E-bike conversions: deposit required (30-50%, exact % still TBD) since parts are ordered from Taiwan
- Refund rule (official): refundable if parts not yet ordered, non-refundable after — though in practice you've bent this rule when you felt bad for people

**Rentals**: Not offered yet, despite having told folks 'next month' — bot should NOT promise a launch date until you decide

**Channels**: WhatsApp (main), Instagram DMs, walk-ins, some phone/email

**Volume**: ~15-20 inquiries/week normally, doubling during CNY season (Jan-Mar)

**Audience**: A real mix — serious cyclists, commuters, e-bike converts, and families

**Languages**: English covers ~90%, Mandarin sometimes needed for older customers (nice-to-have, not essential)

**Escalation**: Everything routes to you first, never directly to Rafiq — you forward technical stuff yourself

**Scope**: Bot answers questions and sends reminders only — no direct booking or payment handling, you keep full control there

**Success looks like**: You stop repeating the same answers (hours, tune-up prices, etc.) dozens of times a week

**Budget**: S$100-200/month, flexible

**Timeline**: ASAP, ideally before next CNY season, but no hard deadline

**Open items for later**: exact e-bike deposit %, e-bike conversion turnaround time (2-5 weeks currently, due to supplier issues), how strictly to state the refund policy, and what to say about rentals until they actually launch.

Does all this look right to you, or is there anything you'd like to add or change?
Mei-Ling Tan

Ooh this looks really good actually! Let me just double check... yeah I think that's basically all right 😊 

Oh wait, one thing — flat tire repair! I don't think I mentioned that one but I say S$15, sometimes S$20 for those. Can we add that in somewhere? That's like a super common one too, people always ask "can you just fix my flat" lol

Everything else looks spot on though, nice job pulling that all together!
Birdie

Perfect, added flat tire repair at S$15-20 — thanks for catching that, Mei-Ling! I've got everything I need now. Thank you so much for walking through all of this with me, it's been great chatting. Next up, this will get handed off to the build team to start putting your chatbot together, and they'll be in touch as things take shape. Enjoy the rest of your day covered in chain grease! 😊
